title: Linux Copy Fail Privilege Escalation and Container Breakout
description: CVE-2026-31431 ("Copy Fail") is a Linux kernel privilege-escalation flaw in the algif_aead component of the AF_ALG userspace cryptographic API. Microsoft reported that an unprivileged local user could corrupt the kernel page cache and obtain root access. Because the page cache is shared across containers on a host, the flaw can support container breakout and host compromise. This package provides container-to-host privilege-escalation detection, hunting and response content for Linux hosts, Kubernetes nodes and CI/CD runners.
campaign_name: Copy Fail Linux kernel privilege escalation (2026)

simulation_steps.title: Unprivileged local execution in container
simulation_steps.description: An unprivileged local or containerized process begins the exploit attempt.

simulation_steps.title: AF_ALG / algif_aead + splice() interaction
simulation_steps.description: Process creates AF_ALG sockets and uses unusual cryptographic-socket and splice() sequences.

simulation_steps.title: Page-cache corruption to root
simulation_steps.description: Controlled page-cache corruption yields root (UID 0) execution.

simulation_steps.title: Escape to host namespace
simulation_steps.description: Because the page cache is shared, the attacker escapes the container boundary to the host.

simulation_steps.title: Detect container-to-host privilege transition
simulation_steps.description: Blue team correlates container AF_ALG socket activity with subsequent root execution or host-namespace access by the same workload.

simulation_steps.title: Drain, patch and rebuild nodes
simulation_steps.description: SOC drains/isolates unpatched nodes, applies kernel updates, refreshes node images and rebuilds on suspected escape.

family_metadata.exposed_surface: Unprivileged local code execution on shared Linux hosts and nodes
